Whoop Peak 5.0 Health and Fitness Tracker — 12 Month Membership Included

The Whoop Peak 5.0 is not a fitness band in the traditional sense. It has no screen, no step count display, no watch face. What it has is something far more valuable — a continuous, 24/7 stream of physiological data from your body, processed by one of the most advanced health analytics platforms in the world, delivered as clear, actionable coaching that tells you exactly what your body needs to perform at its best. WHOOP 5.0 and MG pack more technology into a seven percent smaller form factor. Enhanced sensors capture data 26 times per second, while a redesigned processor delivers 10x more power efficiency — enabling richer insights without sacrificing battery life or comfort.

The Whoop Peak 5.0 comes with a 12 month Peak membership included. The Peak tier ships with the Whoop 5.0 hardware and unlocks the advanced health, stress and longevity features including Healthspan and Pace of Aging, Health Monitor with health alerts and Real-time Stress Monitor. This is Whoop's most complete fitness and health tracking package for serious athletes, active professionals and anyone who wants to understand their body at a deeper level than any other wearable on the market offers.

Why Whoop Is Different From Every Other Fitness Tracker

Most fitness bands tell you what happened. Whoop tells you what it means and what to do about it. The difference sounds simple but in practice it is transformative for how you train, recover and live.

When you wear a standard fitness tracker, you see steps, calories and heart rate. When you wear the Whoop 5.0 Peak, you see three numbers that actually drive performance decisions: your Strain score, your Recovery score and your Sleep Performance score. These three metrics, updated daily and tracked continuously, give you a complete picture of how hard your body is working, how well it is recovering from that work and how effectively your sleep is restoring it. Whoop simplifies and labels your activity differently in the app, providing a summary Sleep, Recovery and Strain score to sum up your progress in three values. When contrasted with a Recovery value, which is determined by stress and sleep patterns, you get easy-to-understand values that offer a quick check-in on health and fitness.

Strain Score — Know Exactly How Hard You Are Pushing

The Strain value that Whoop generates is a valuable tool for understanding how hard you have been working. Strain is measured on a scale from 0 to 21 and accounts for every physical effort you make throughout the day — your gym session, your walk, your stress levels, your commute, your workday. It is not just counting steps or calories burned. It is measuring the cumulative cardiovascular load on your body from everything you do. From daily steps and VO₂ Max to Muscular Strain during strength training and 145 plus supported activities, members can now optimise fitness for both performance and long-term health outcomes.

For Pakistani athletes and gym-goers training in Karachi and Lahore's heat, where sessions in 35-40 degree temperatures place significantly more cardiovascular load on the body than the same workout in a cooler climate, Strain score is particularly relevant. Your body is working harder just to regulate temperature. Whoop accounts for this in its data. Your Strain on a hot outdoor workout day will accurately reflect the true load — not just the physical exertion but the thermal stress your cardiovascular system is managing simultaneously.

Recovery Score — The Number That Should Drive Every Training Decision

Recovery is measured each morning as a percentage from 0 to 100 based on your heart rate variability, resting heart rate, sleep performance and respiratory rate from the previous night. It tells you in a single number whether your body is ready to take on high strain, should keep things moderate or genuinely needs rest.

This is where Whoop changes how serious athletes train. Most people make training decisions based on motivation, schedule or habit. Whoop makes the decision data-driven. Notifications like approaching bedtime, caffeine cutoffs and when recovery was maximised and ready to push harder were excellent cues to help reach goals. A green Recovery score above 67 means your body is primed for a high-effort session. An orange score between 34 and 66 means moderate activity is appropriate. A red score below 33 means your body is telling you to rest, and pushing through that red number consistently is one of the most reliable paths to overtraining, injury and burnout.

For Pakistani fitness enthusiasts who train through Ramadan, during exam stress periods or across demanding work schedules, Recovery score is the objective measure that removes the guesswork from whether today is a training day or a rest day.

Sleep Performance Score — More Than Just Hours

In 2025, WHOOP set a new standard for sleep tracking — combining clinical-grade validation with smarter, more actionable guidance. The updated Sleep Performance Score offers a holistic view of your rest, factoring in sleep sufficiency, consistency, efficiency and stress to show how well your body truly recovered overnight. This is not just counting how many hours you slept. Whoop tracks sleep stages — light, deep and REM — and evaluates the quality of each stage, not just the duration. It tells you what percentage of the sleep you needed you actually got, whether your sleep was consistent with your normal patterns and how your overnight stress levels affected recovery quality.

Whoop also gives you a specific sleep recommendation each night based on your day's Strain, your current Recovery debt and your personal sleep patterns. If you trained hard today, Whoop will tell you to sleep more tonight. If you have been carrying a sleep debt across the week, it adjusts the recommendation upward. It functions as a genuine sleep coach, not just a sleep recorder.

Real-Time Stress Monitor — Unique to Peak Membership

Whoop Peak members have access to a real-time stress monitor, where users can see their stress level and complete guided breathing sessions if they would like to lower it. Stress is one of the most underestimated factors in athletic performance and health. Chronic work stress, exam pressure or life stress all raise cortisol, which suppresses recovery, disrupts sleep and reduces HRV — which in turn reduces your ability to adapt to training and perform. Most fitness trackers ignore stress entirely. Whoop Peak monitors it continuously and gives you a live readout so you can see in real time how your body is responding to different situations throughout the day.

The guided breathing sessions integrated into the real-time stress monitor are not just a wellness add-on. Lowering stress actively and measurably improves HRV, which directly improves your next Recovery score, which directly improves your training capacity. For Pakistani professionals managing demanding work schedules alongside ambitious training goals, this feature creates a feedback loop between stress management and fitness performance that no other wearable provides.

Healthspan and Pace of Aging — Unique to Peak Membership

Powered by nine key metrics across sleep, activity and fitness — including VO₂ Max, resting heart rate, sleep consistency and strength activity — Healthspan connects the dots between daily habits and biological trajectory. It reveals how recovery, training and lifestyle decisions affect overall vitality and helps you take action to improve it over time. WHOOP updates your WHOOP Age and Pace of Aging weekly, so you can see exactly how your body is trending and what changes are making a difference. This is Whoop's most ambitious feature — developed in partnership with the Buck Institute for Research on Aging — and it answers the question that matters beyond fitness performance: are my daily habits making me healthier or less healthy over time?

Menstrual Cycle Insights — Training With Your Body Not Against It

Women's Hormonal Insights empowers women to take control of their health with deeper, more personalised data on how hormones shape performance, recovery and wellbeing. Menstrual Cycle Insights integrates menstrual cycle tracking with physiological data, connecting hormonal changes to shifts in sleep, strain, mood and recovery. You can log symptoms, track phases and receive educational guidance within each stage of your cycle. For women who train seriously, understanding how their hormonal cycle affects their recovery capacity, sleep quality and optimal training intensity is one of the most powerful tools available for sustainable athletic improvement. Whoop Peak makes this data visible and actionable in a way that no other fitness wearable currently provides.

Health Monitor — Vitals at a Glance

Whoop Peak members have access to a Health Monitor feature, which provides a quick look at vitals like respiratory rate, heart rate, blood oxygen and skin temperature. These four metrics, tracked continuously and compared against your personal baselines, are powerful early indicators of illness, overtraining and physiological stress. Skin temperature elevations often precede illness symptoms by 24 to 48 hours. Resting heart rate elevation combined with HRV depression is a reliable signal of overtraining. Blood oxygen drops can indicate sleep quality issues or early illness. Whoop surfaces these signals before they become problems.

VO₂ Max — Your Cardiovascular Fitness Score

With the launch of VO₂ Max, WHOOP introduced a new way to understand long-term cardiovascular fitness and its connection to overall healthspan. VO₂ Max is the single most predictive metric for long-term cardiovascular health and athletic performance potential. Whoop calculates yours continuously from your heart rate data during exercise and at rest, tracking how it changes over time as your fitness improves. For Pakistani athletes looking to track genuine fitness progress beyond just how heavy they can lift or how fast they can run, VO₂ Max gives you the most objective measure of cardiovascular improvement available without laboratory testing.

Whoop Coach — Your Personal AI Trainer

Using Whoop Coach is like being able to text your own private personal trainer. The presentation of data, interlaced with tips and coaching, is fantastic. Whoop helped interpret data to know if performance was improving, on average or decreasing. The app provides clear feedback as well as AI coaching that can help the user identify when sleep, nutrition or workouts are having a beneficial impact on overall health and prescriptive guidance on how to train or recover even better. Whoop Coach analyses your full data history and answers questions in natural language — why is my recovery low this week, what should I do today, how has my sleep changed since I started training, how do I improve my HRV. It is the only fitness tracker that gives you a coach who knows your entire health and performance history and can give you personalised answers based on it.

14 Plus Days Battery Life — Wear It Always

Whoop 5.0 supports 14 days of battery life, which is around triple the four-to-five-day range offered by Whoop 4.0. The reason 14 days matters is that Whoop is only useful if you wear it all the time. Missing a night of sleep data breaks your Recovery score. Missing workouts breaks your Strain data. The 14-day battery means you charge it once every two weeks, using the slide-on battery charger that charges the device while you are still wearing it — no taking it off, no gaps in data. For Pakistani users who travel frequently between cities, 14 days means you complete most trips without needing to charge at all.

No Screen — By Design

The absence of a screen is one of the most deliberate and important design decisions Whoop has made. Without a screen, there are no notifications pulling your attention away from your workout or your sleep. There is no reason to check the device during a set or in the middle of the night. The data lives in the app, reviewed intentionally when you choose to, rather than interrupting your day constantly. The Whoop is a unique device for fitness and lifestyle tracking that emphasises minimalism and 24/7 wearability. The result is a tracker you genuinely wear 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including in the shower and pool, collecting continuous data without ever becoming a distraction.

  • Battery Life: 14 plus days
  • Sensors: Heart rate, HRV, SpO2, skin temperature, respiratory rate, accelerometer
  • Data Rate: 26 times per second

Whoop Life MG Health and Fitness Tracker — 12 Month Membership Included

The Whoop Life MG is the most advanced health and fitness wearable Whoop has ever built. While the Whoop Peak 5.0 is built for athletes and performance-focused individuals, the Whoop Life MG is built for people who want to go a step further — monitoring not just how their body is performing, but how their heart is actually functioning. The Whoop Life tier comes with the Whoop MG hardware and encompasses the full suite of features, including ECG, Heart Screener, AFib Detection and Blood Pressure Insights. This is a different class of wearable from everything else on the market, and a fundamentally different proposition from any fitness tracker available in Pakistan today.

The Whoop Life tier is the most powerful Whoop ever, delivering medical-grade health and performance insights at its core. The 12 month Life membership included with this product unlocks every feature Whoop offers — from the foundational Strain, Recovery and Sleep scores through to on-demand ECG, daily blood pressure readings and priority access to frontier health tools as Whoop continues to develop its platform.

Whoop MG — What Medical Grade Actually Means

The "MG" in Whoop MG stands for medical grade. This is not just marketing language. The hardware inside the Whoop MG contains sensors and circuitry that the standard Whoop 5.0 does not have — specifically the components needed to capture the electrical activity of the heart for ECG readings and the advanced skin temperature sensor that improves the accuracy of hormonal insights and the Health Monitor feature.

The Whoop MG uses a scalloped edge design and captures advanced health metrics including ECG measurements, blood pressure insights and irregular heart rhythm notifications. It also features an advanced skin temperature sensor. The scalloped edge design is not just aesthetic — it positions the ECG-conductive elements of the clasp correctly against the wrist and provides a surface that conducts the electrical signal needed for a valid ECG reading. Every physical design decision on the MG serves the medical-grade function of the hardware.

Heart Screener With ECG — Your Heart, In Your Hands

Whoop now includes an FDA-cleared ECG feature that allows a reading to be taken anytime, from your wrist and shared directly with a healthcare provider. The Heart Screener detects signs of Atrial Fibrillation, a leading cause of stroke, and provides Irregular Heart Rhythm Notifications for greater peace of mind.

Taking an ECG reading is straightforward. Open the Heart Screener tool in the Whoop app, place your thumb and index finger on the ECG-conductive clasp of the MG band and hold for 30 seconds. The reading reports either normal sinus rhythm or flags an irregular rhythm such as AFib. The report can be saved and shared directly with a cardiologist or general physician, providing the kind of documentation that supports a professional medical consultation without requiring a clinic visit or an expensive standalone ECG device.

Atrial Fibrillation is particularly relevant for the Pakistani population. AFib is one of the most common cardiac arrhythmias globally and one of the leading causes of stroke. It is frequently undetected because it is intermittent — it may not be present during a standard ECG at a clinic, which captures only a few seconds of heart activity. Wearing the Whoop MG 24 hours a day means your heart rhythm is being passively monitored continuously, and the on-demand ECG gives you the ability to capture a reading at the exact moment you feel a symptom like palpitations, chest discomfort or unusual breathlessness.

Irregular Heart Rhythm Notifications — Passive Background Monitoring

Beyond on-demand ECG readings, the Whoop MG monitors your heart rhythm passively in the background throughout the day and night. Irregular Heart Rhythm Notifications are provided for greater peace of mind, detecting signs of Atrial Fibrillation continuously. You do not need to initiate a reading for the device to detect an irregularity. If the MG's background monitoring picks up a pattern that suggests AFib, you receive a notification prompting you to take a confirmatory ECG reading. For anyone with a family history of cardiac conditions, or who has previously experienced palpitations or unexplained fatigue, this passive monitoring provides a level of reassurance that no other wearable in Pakistan's market currently offers.

Blood Pressure Insights — Daily Readings From Your Wrist

Blood pressure is a critical indicator of heart and vascular health. Unlike a blood pressure cuff, Whoop MG allows you to monitor blood pressure trends continuously and provides you with a daily reading each morning. To unlock Blood Pressure Insights, you log a traditional cuff-reading as a baseline calibration in the app. From that point, the MG's overnight biometric analysis generates an estimated systolic and diastolic range each morning based on your HRV, heart rate patterns and skin temperature data from the previous night.

It is important to be clear about what this feature is and what it is not. Blood Pressure Insights is not a medical device and does not provide medical advice. It is a wellness trend monitoring tool, currently in beta. It is designed to help you understand how your daily habits — sleep quality, exercise, alcohol, stress — affect your blood pressure trends over time, not to diagnose or treat hypertension. For Pakistani adults who want to track how their lifestyle choices impact their cardiovascular wellness on a daily basis without visiting a clinic each time, this feature adds a genuinely new dimension to health self-awareness.

Everything in Peak, Plus Medical Grade

The Whoop Life membership includes every feature available in the Peak tier, plus the medical-grade additions exclusive to the MG. That means you also get:

Strain and Recovery Scores

The core engine of Whoop's coaching system. Strain measures the cumulative cardiovascular load on your body across the full day. Recovery, calculated each morning from HRV, resting heart rate, sleep performance and respiratory rate, tells you in a single score from 0 to 100 whether your body is ready to push hard, maintain moderate activity or genuinely needs rest. For Pakistani athletes training through summer heat, Ramadan or demanding work schedules, these two scores create a data-driven training framework that removes guesswork from every day.

Healthspan and Pace of Aging

Healthspan is powered by nine key metrics across sleep, activity and fitness including VO₂ Max, resting heart rate, sleep consistency and strength activity. It reveals how recovery, training and lifestyle decisions affect overall vitality. WHOOP updates your WHOOP Age and Pace of Aging weekly so you can see exactly how your body is trending and what changes are making a difference. For Whoop Life members, Healthspan becomes even more powerful because blood pressure trend data and cardiac rhythm data from the MG feed into the overall longevity picture alongside the standard nine metrics.

Real-Time Stress Monitor

Monitors your physiological stress level continuously throughout the day and provides guided breathing sessions to actively lower it. For Life members the stress data is also integrated with the cardiovascular monitoring, giving you a fuller picture of how acute stress events affect your heart rate patterns and HRV in real time.

Health Monitor With Alerts

Health Monitor provides a quick look at vitals like respiratory rate, heart rate, blood oxygen and skin temperature. The advanced skin temperature sensor in the MG hardware improves the accuracy of this feature compared to the Whoop 5.0, particularly for hormonal insight tracking where skin temperature fluctuations are a key biometric signal.

Sleep Performance Score

Updated for 2025 with clinical-grade validation, the Sleep Performance Score evaluates sleep sufficiency, consistency, efficiency and overnight stress — not just hours slept. The algorithm was trained on polysomnography data, the gold standard of sleep measurement. For Life members, the overnight data captured while you sleep also feeds into the blood pressure insight calculation and the cardiac rhythm passive monitoring, making every night of sleep data genuinely multifunctional.

Menstrual Cycle and Pregnancy Insights

Women's Hormonal Insights empowers women to take control of their health with deeper, more personalised data on how hormones shape performance, recovery and wellbeing. Pregnancy Insights provides weekly tailored insights into how the body adapts through pregnancy, helping you adjust activity, rest and hydration. The advanced skin temperature sensor in the MG hardware makes these hormonal insights more accurate for Life members than for Peak members using the standard 5.0 sensor.

VO₂ Max and 145 Plus Activity Tracking

Continuous VO₂ Max tracking giving you the most objective available measure of cardiovascular fitness improvement over time. Support for 145 plus activities including strength training with muscular strain differentiation, making the Whoop Life relevant across every form of exercise — gym training, running, swimming, yoga and sport-specific training.

Whoop Coach

AI-powered personal coaching that analyses your full data history — including your cardiac and blood pressure data as a Life member — and answers questions in natural language about your health, training and recovery. The most comprehensive coaching context available in any wearable on the market.

Priority Access to Frontier Health Features

The Life tier is where more frontier health tools will arrive first. Advanced Labs will allow people to book blood testing through Whoop and integrate the results with wearable data, enabling analysis of 60 to 70 biomarkers integrated with your 24/7 wearable data. For Life members, Advanced Labs creates a bridge between wearable biometrics and blood panel data — connecting what your body is doing every second with what your blood chemistry reveals about what is happening at a cellular and hormonal level. This is the closest a consumer wearable has ever come to giving you the kind of comprehensive health picture previously only available through clinical testing programmes.

Who the Whoop Life MG Is For

The Whoop Life MG is the right choice for several specific groups of people in Pakistan:

Anyone with a personal or family history of cardiac conditions who wants daily passive cardiac monitoring and the ability to take an ECG reading on demand at any time without a clinic visit.

High-performing professionals and executives in Pakistani cities who manage significant work stress alongside fitness goals and want the most complete picture of how both are affecting their cardiovascular health and longevity.

Serious athletes who want every feature Whoop offers — including the most accurate hormonal insights through the advanced skin temperature sensor — to optimise performance, recovery and long-term health simultaneously.

Anyone over 35 who is investing seriously in their long-term health and wants objective, weekly data on whether their biological age is tracking younger or older than their chronological age, and what specific habits are driving that trajectory.

14 Plus Days Battery Life on MG Hardware

The new hardware offers 14 plus days of battery life across Whoop 5.0 and MG. Members with the Wireless PowerPack have access to a full month of battery life. The Wireless PowerPack slides over the MG band and charges the device while you are wearing it, meaning the device never needs to come off for charging. For a device performing continuous cardiac monitoring and blood pressure analysis throughout the day and night, uninterrupted wear is not just convenient — it is essential for the data continuity that makes the insights accurate.

What is the difference between the Lavender Blue and Berry Pink Fitbit Air?

The technology, sensors, health features, battery life and AI coaching are identical across all Fitbit Air colourways. The difference is purely in the colour and buckle finish. The Lavender Blue edition comes with a polished silver stainless steel buckle while the Berry Pink comes with a polished champagne gold buckle. The Lavender Blue is the more neutral, versatile everyday option that pairs naturally with silver jewellery and works with a wider range of outfit colours. The Berry Pink is the bolder, warmer option suited to rose gold accessories and feminine styling.

Do I need to pay a monthly subscription to use the Fitbit Air?

Most core health features work without any subscription. Google Health Premium is optional, unlocking the Gemini-powered AI Health Coach and advanced personalised plans. Core features available for free include 24/7 heart rate, sleep stages and Sleep Score, SpO2, skin temperature variation, Cardio Load, Readiness Score and AFib detection. The Gemini-powered Health Coach, adaptive workout planning and AI-driven sleep coaching require Google Health Premium. Three months of Premium are included free with the Fitbit Air, giving you full access to evaluate whether the coaching adds enough value for you to continue the subscription.

Does the Fitbit Air have built-in GPS?

The Fitbit Air does not have built-in GPS. Outdoor activity route tracking requires your paired smartphone to be carried with you. If you run or cycle outdoors and want route mapping, bring your phone and the Fitbit Air will use it for GPS data. Heart rate, pace and workout tracking all work independently of GPS. If built-in GPS is essential for your training, the Whoop Peak or a GPS-equipped smartwatch would be more appropriate. For indoor training, urban walking and gym sessions — which are the primary activities for most Pakistani fitness enthusiasts — GPS is not needed for meaningful health tracking.

How accurate is the AFib detection on the Fitbit Air?

Google Fitbit Air tracks your heart rhythm while you are still or sleeping and looks out for signs of atrial fibrillation. The passive AFib detection is most accurate during stillness and sleep when the optical sensor can maintain consistent contact and blood flow is stable. It is not a substitute for a clinical ECG diagnosis, and an alert from the device should prompt a medical consultation rather than be treated as a definitive diagnosis. For users who want on-demand ECG capability in addition to passive monitoring, the Whoop Life MG offers FDA-cleared on-demand ECG readings. The Fitbit Air's AFib monitoring is passive background monitoring designed to flag patterns that warrant further investigation.

Can I wear the Fitbit Air while swimming?

Yes. The Fitbit Air resists water up to 50 metres, rated at 5 ATM water resistance. It is suitable for swimming, showering, water sports and daily activities in rain or humidity. The Performance Loop Band is also designed to handle moisture without degrading. Pakistan's coastal climate in Karachi and the frequent use of swimming as a fitness activity make this level of water resistance practically important for everyday wearability.

How does the Fitbit Air work alongside a Pixel Watch?

For the first time, you can pair both a Pixel Watch and a Fitbit Air to the same Google Health account simultaneously. Wear your Pixel Watch during the day for screen access and notifications, switch to the lightweight screenless Fitbit Air at night for uninterrupted sleep tracking. Both devices sync to the same Google Health account automatically. This dual-device setup gives you the best of both worlds — a full-featured smartwatch for daytime use and a featherlight health tracker for sleep — without duplicating data or managing two separate apps.

What is the Cardio Load feature and why does it matter?

Cardio Load tracks the cumulative cardiovascular stress of your training over a rolling period, not just the effort of a single session. Google Fitbit Air measures your Cardio Load then gives you a daily goal that helps you perform your best. When your Cardio Load is rising steadily relative to your recovery capacity, it means you are building fitness. When it spikes sharply — from a sudden increase in training volume or intensity — it signals overtraining risk. The Readiness Score combines Cardio Load with your overnight recovery data to give you a daily training recommendation that responds to how your body is actually coping, not just to your training schedule on paper.

Is a Google account required to use the Fitbit Air?

Yes. A Google account is required to set up and pair the Google Fitbit Air with the Google Health app. If you do not have a Google account, you can create one free of charge. You do not need a Gmail address as your primary email — any email address can be used to create a Google account. The Google Health app is available on both Android and iOS and works fully on iPhones, so iPhone users can use the Fitbit Air without any limitation.

How does the Fitbit Air compare to the Whoop Peak 5.0 for sleep tracking?

Both are excellent sleep trackers that go significantly beyond basic hours-slept recording. The Fitbit Air uses Google's Gemini-powered Health Coach to provide actionable sleep coaching and adaptive plans based on your patterns. The Whoop Peak 5.0 uses an algorithm trained on polysomnography data and integrates sleep quality directly into its Recovery score for next-day training guidance. The Fitbit Air does not require a subscription for core sleep tracking. The Whoop Peak requires an active membership to access any data. For someone starting out with health tracking and wanting a lower commitment entry point, the Fitbit Air is the more accessible choice. For athletes who want deeper performance-focused recovery analytics, the Whoop Peak is the stronger platform.

Google Fitbit Air Obsidian Black Screenless Fitness and Health Tracker

The Google Fitbit Air in Obsidian Black is the most versatile and universally wearable colourway in the Fitbit Air range. The deep matte black finish with a matte black stainless steel buckle is clean, minimal and works with everything. It looks equally at home on the wrist of a man hitting the gym at Karachi's Defence or a woman heading to a corporate meeting in Lahore's Gulberg. It does not look like a fitness tracker. It does not look like a smartwatch. It looks like a considered, modern accessory that happens to be quietly collecting some of the most useful health data available in any consumer wearable today.

The Fitbit Air is simple, affordable and comfortable enough to wear 24/7. It was designed to unlock the full power of the Google Health Coach with Google Health Premium, bringing personal health insights and recommendations to everyone. This is not a product for a specific type of person. It is a product for anyone who wants to understand their body better without being distracted by a screen on their wrist all day.

The Obsidian Black Colourway and What Makes It Different

The Obsidian Black Fitbit Air is the only colourway in the range that is built around a matte aesthetic throughout. Where the Berry Pink has a champagne gold buckle and the Lavender Blue has a polished silver buckle, the Obsidian Black carries the matte finish through to the hardware itself. The result is a unified, monochromatic look that is genuinely gender-neutral and complements both casual and formal wear without any adjustment.

The Elevated Modern Band is available in Obsidian colourway. This optional upgrade band transforms the Fitbit Air from a fitness tracker into something that reads as a fashionable bracelet in a formal or professional setting. For Pakistani professionals who wear their Fitbit Air to work and want an accessory that transitions seamlessly from the gym to the boardroom, the Obsidian Elevated Modern Band is the best combination of the Fitbit Air range.

Designed for People Who Are Tired of Being Distracted

It sits silently on your wrist with a screenless design built so you can live in the moment. You have the freedom to explore deep insights from the Google Health app on your phone when you want them and stay notification-free when you do not. Every smartwatch and conventional fitness tracker in Pakistan's market today competes for your attention. Notifications, step counts on your wrist, messages buzzing through, app alerts flashing. The Fitbit Air reverses this entirely. It collects everything and says nothing. You go about your day completely undisturbed, and when you choose to check your data you open the Google Health app and find a complete, detailed picture of everything your body did since you last looked.

For people in Pakistan managing demanding work schedules, family responsibilities and a fitness goal simultaneously, removing one more source of distraction from their day is not a small thing. The Fitbit Air makes that removal effortless because the data collection never stops, even when the notifications do.

What the Fitbit Air Obsidian Tracks Every Day

24/7 Heart Rate and Active Zone Minutes

The Fitbit Air is a proactive wellness partner that uses high-fidelity sensor technology in a tiny, discreet pebble that enables advanced health and fitness tracking like 24/7 heart rate, heart rhythm monitoring with AFib alerts, SpO2, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, sleep stages and duration, and more. Active Zone Minutes measure the time you spend with your heart rate elevated into fat burn, cardio or peak zones. This is a fundamentally more useful metric than step count for anyone trying to improve cardiovascular fitness or manage weight, because it tells you how much of your daily movement was intense enough to produce a meaningful physiological response rather than just counting every shuffle and stroll the same way.

Cardio Load and Readiness Score

You can start a workout from the app, follow along with a coach-recommended guided workout or simply get going and the Fitbit Air will detect and track common activities automatically, sending you a recap of your workout. The automatic detection gets better over time and is personalised to you. Your Cardio Load tracks the cumulative training stress your body has absorbed over recent days. When Cardio Load builds progressively it means your fitness is improving. When it spikes beyond your recovery capacity it signals overtraining. Your Readiness Score synthesises Cardio Load with overnight HRV and sleep quality into a single daily number telling you whether to push hard today or pull back. For gym-goers in Karachi and Lahore who train five or six days a week, this daily Readiness Score is the objective check that prevents the overtraining mistakes that derail progress.

Heart Rate Variability During Sleep

HRV is the single most reliable indicator of physiological recovery available to a wrist-worn sensor, and the Fitbit Air measures it throughout your sleep when the body is at rest and the optical sensors are most accurate. A high HRV overnight indicates your body recovered well. A low HRV indicates accumulated fatigue, illness onset, high stress or poor sleep quality. The Fitbit Air surfaces this data each morning in the Google Health app as part of your Readiness Score calculation, giving you the biological context behind how you feel and whether to act on it or push through.

Blood Oxygen SpO2 Monitoring

The Fitbit Air tracks SpO2 blood oxygen levels using red and infrared sensors for 24/7 monitoring. SpO2 monitoring overnight flags drops in blood oxygen that indicate disrupted breathing during sleep. Persistent SpO2 dips are one of the primary indicators of sleep apnoea, which is significantly underdiagnosed across Pakistan despite being a common condition. Having months of nightly SpO2 data from the Fitbit Air gives a doctor genuinely useful information to work with when a consultation does happen, rather than relying on a self-reported description of symptoms.

Skin Temperature Variation

Overnight skin temperature is tracked continuously against your personal baseline. Deviations upward often appear 24 to 48 hours before the visible symptoms of illness, giving you an early warning that your body is fighting something before you feel it. Skin temperature data also contributes to the Readiness Score calculation as an input reflecting overall physiological stress. For women, the nightly temperature tracking connects to cycle phase awareness, with warmer temperatures in the luteal phase and cooler temperatures in the follicular phase creating a passive hormonal signal that the Google Health app surfaces over time.

AFib Detection During Rest and Sleep

The Fitbit Air tracks your heart rhythm while you are still or sleeping and looks out for signs of atrial fibrillation. AFib is frequently present without any symptoms and often only detected incidentally during a routine checkup or not until a more serious event like a stroke has occurred. Passive nightly monitoring through the Fitbit Air dramatically increases the probability of detecting an irregular rhythm pattern that warrants medical investigation, because it checks your rhythm every night rather than for a few seconds during an occasional clinic visit.

Sleep Tracking and Sleep Score

The Fitbit Air tracks light, deep and REM sleep stages throughout every night and generates a Sleep Score each morning. The Google Health Coach analyses your sleep patterns across weeks and builds personalised coaching around what it finds. Google Health Coach goes beyond tracking your sleep to help you understand your sleep patterns and how to improve them, with weekly spotlights to help you understand and improve your sleep. For Pakistani users whose sleep is disrupted by heat in summer, noise from urban environments or the late schedules common in family and social life, the coaching responds to your actual sleep patterns rather than delivering generic advice that does not account for your specific circumstances.

Workout Detection and Gym Tracking

The Fitbit Air detects and tracks common activities automatically, sending you a recap of your workout. It also lets you snap a photo of your cardio equipment or the circuit training routine on the whiteboard at the gym for the Health Coach to incorporate into your plan. The photo-based workout logging is a genuinely novel feature for gym users. Instead of manually entering your exercises, you take a photo of the gym whiteboard or the machine display and the Gemini-powered Health Coach reads and records it. For Pakistani gym-goers doing coached group sessions or circuit training where the exercises change regularly, this removes one of the most friction-heavy parts of workout logging entirely.

The Gemini Health Coach and Why It Is Built Differently

The Gemini-powered Google Health Coach takes your sleep data, activity data, heart rate trends and recovery scores and turns them into personalised daily action plans. It builds adaptive workout plans, suggests recovery windows, analyses sleep disruptions and answers health questions in natural conversation. The coaching adapts continuously as it learns more about how your body responds. It does not hand you a fixed 8-week plan and leave you to it. It adjusts this week based on last week's recovery scores, your current Cardio Load trajectory and the sleep patterns it has observed. It celebrates improvements, flags concerning trends and answers questions in plain conversational language through the app.

In some regions, Google Health lets you connect medical records to your profile. The Health Coach can then factor in your medical history when making recommendations. This is a bigger differentiator than it sounds as no competing wearable platform offers this. As this feature expands to more markets, Fitbit Air users with connected medical records will have coaching that accounts for diagnosed conditions, previous injuries and prescriptions in a way that generic fitness platforms simply cannot replicate.

No Mandatory Subscription and Why That Matters

Every Whoop product requires an active subscription to access any data at all. The Fitbit Air does not. Core tracking data including heart rate, sleep, steps, SpO2, skin temperature, Cardio Load and Readiness Score are all available free. Google Health Premium unlocks the Gemini-powered Health Coach. Three months free with Fitbit Air purchase. For Pakistani buyers who are wary of committing to an ongoing subscription for a product they have not fully tested, the Fitbit Air's free core tracking removes that barrier entirely. Three months of the full Premium experience is included with every purchase, which gives you enough time to decide whether the AI coaching is worth continuing before any payment is required.

Swappable Bands for Every Situation

The Obsidian Black Fitbit Air ships with the Performance Loop Band in Obsidian. The Active Band in sweatproof, wetproof silicone is perfect for high-intensity training. The Elevated Modern Band transforms the device from a fitness tracker into a fashionable bracelet with classic colours that blend with any style. The pebble pod pops out and snaps into any compatible band in seconds. For Pakistani men and women who move between gym sessions, formal work environments and social settings throughout the day, having three band options that serve three completely different aesthetic needs from the same device is a genuine practical advantage.
